dry_skin.name: Dry Skin
dry_skin.description: Skin that feels tight, flaky, or lacking in oils. Commonly supported with humectants and barrier lipids.
dry_skin.usage_guidance: Use a gentle cleanser, layer a hydrating serum on damp skin, then seal with a ceramide-rich moisturizer. Avoid harsh foaming washes.
warnings: Avoid high-strength acids or retinoids until the barrier feels more comfortable.

ingredients.name: Hyaluronic Acid
ingredients.benefit: May help attract and hold water so skin feels more hydrated.
ingredients.usage: Apply to damp skin in the morning and evening.

ingredients.name: Ceramides
ingredients.benefit: Can support the skin barrier and help reduce moisture loss.
ingredients.usage: Look for in moisturizer, morning and night.

ingredients.name: Glycerin
ingredients.benefit: A common humectant that may help draw moisture into the skin.
ingredients.usage: Often in cleansers and moisturizers; use daily.

ingredients.name: Squalane
ingredients.benefit: A lightweight oil that may help soften dry-feeling skin.
ingredients.usage: Use in moisturizer or as a few drops at night.

dehydrated_skin.name: Dehydrated Skin
dehydrated_skin.description: Skin that lacks water (can still look oily). Often feels tight after cleansing.
dehydrated_skin.usage_guidance: Focus on water-binding ingredients, then seal with moisturizer. Drink water and avoid over-cleansing.
warnings: Dehydration is different from dry (oil-poor) skin; lightweight gels can still help oily-dehydrated skin.

ingredients.name: Hyaluronic Acid
ingredients.benefit: May help the skin hold onto water.
ingredients.usage: Apply to damp skin, then moisturizer.

ingredients.name: Glycerin
ingredients.benefit: Can support hydration in cleansers and leave-on products.

ingredients.name: Ceramides
ingredients.benefit: May help keep hydration from evaporating.

dullness.name: Dullness
dullness.description: Skin that looks tired, lifeless, or lacking glow.
dullness.usage_guidance: Daily sunscreen plus a gentle antioxidant in the morning is commonly used to support a brighter-looking complexion.
warnings: Vitamin C can sting very sensitive skin; start with a lower-strength or derivative formula.

ingredients.name: Vitamin C
ingredients.benefit: Commonly used to support a brighter-looking appearance.
ingredients.caution: Can irritate sensitive skin; patch test.

ingredients.name: Niacinamide
ingredients.benefit: May help improve the look of uneven, tired-looking skin.
ingredients.usage: Morning or night, 2–5% if new to it.

ingredients.name: Alpha Arbutin
ingredients.benefit: Can support a more even-looking tone over time.
ingredients.usage: Night or morning on clean skin.

uneven_skin_tone.name: Uneven Skin Tone
uneven_skin_tone.description: Patchy or blotchy-looking tone. Often discussed with discoloration, not a medical diagnosis.
uneven_skin_tone.usage_guidance: Consistent sunscreen is essential. Pair with niacinamide or vitamin C. Avoid stacking many brightening actives at once.
warnings: Daily SPF is important when using brightening ingredients.

ingredients.name: Niacinamide
ingredients.benefit: May help the appearance of uneven tone.

ingredients.name: Vitamin C
ingredients.benefit: Commonly used to support a more even-looking complexion.
ingredients.caution: Can sting; start slowly if sensitive.

ingredients.name: Alpha Arbutin
ingredients.benefit: Can support the look of discoloration over time.

dark_spots.name: Dark Spots
dark_spots.description: Marks or patches that look darker than surrounding skin, including marks that appear after breakouts.
dark_spots.usage_guidance: Use sunscreen every morning. Introduce one brightening ingredient at a time.
warnings: Do not combine several strong brighteners plus acids without buffering. Results take weeks, not days.

ingredients.name: Vitamin C
ingredients.benefit: May help improve the appearance of dark spots with consistent use and SPF.
ingredients.caution: Can irritate; patch test.

ingredients.name: Alpha Arbutin
ingredients.benefit: Commonly used to support a more even-looking tone.

ingredients.name: Azelaic Acid
ingredients.benefit: Can support the look of marks and redness in some routines.
ingredients.usage: Start a few nights per week, 10% leave-on if tolerated.
ingredients.caution: May tingle; stop if persistent burning.

acne.name: Acne
acne.description: Breakouts such as pimples. This is not a diagnosis of acne severity or type.
acne.usage_guidance: Keep cleanser gentle. Use one pore-clearing or calming active, then moisturizer. Do not pick.
warnings: Avoid stacking salicylic acid, benzoyl peroxide, and retinoids on the same night.
Cystic, painful, or scarring breakouts should be reviewed by a dermatologist.

ingredients.name: Salicylic Acid
ingredients.benefit: Commonly used to help keep pores clearer-looking.
ingredients.usage: Start 2–3 nights per week, then increase if tolerated.
ingredients.caution: Can dry or peel; do not combine with retinoids at first.

ingredients.name: Niacinamide
ingredients.benefit: May help the look of oiliness and post-breakout marks.

ingredients.name: Azelaic Acid
ingredients.benefit: Can support the appearance of breakouts and uneven tone.
ingredients.usage: Night, a few times per week to start.
ingredients.caution: May tingle. Not a prescription.

oily_skin.name: Oily Skin
oily_skin.description: Skin that looks shiny or feels greasy, especially in the T-zone.
oily_skin.usage_guidance: Use a gentle gel cleanser, lightweight moisturizer, and oil-balancing ingredients. Skipping moisturizer can increase shine for some people.
warnings: Avoid harsh stripping washes that leave skin tight.

ingredients.name: Niacinamide
ingredients.benefit: May help the appearance of excess oil over time.
ingredients.usage: Daily serum, 5% is a common starting range.

ingredients.name: Salicylic Acid
ingredients.benefit: Commonly used for an oilier, more congested look.
ingredients.usage: A few times per week at night.
ingredients.caution: Can over-dry if used daily with other actives.

ingredients.name: Zinc PCA
ingredients.benefit: Can support a less shiny-looking finish in some formulas.
ingredients.usage: Often in lightweight serums or moisturizers.

excess_oil.name: Excess Oil
excess_oil.description: Visible shine or sebum that feels like it returns quickly after cleansing.
excess_oil.usage_guidance: Lightweight, non-comedogenic moisturizer plus niacinamide is commonly used. Blotting papers can help during the day.
warnings: Over-exfoliating can worsen oiliness for some people.

ingredients.name: Niacinamide
ingredients.benefit: May help the look of oiliness.

ingredients.name: Salicylic Acid
ingredients.benefit: Can support clearer-looking pores in oily areas.
ingredients.caution: Do not stack with retinoids at first.

ingredients.name: Zinc PCA
ingredients.benefit: Sometimes used to support a more balanced-looking finish.

blackheads.name: Blackheads
blackheads.description: Open clogged pores that look dark on the surface.
blackheads.usage_guidance: Consistent BHA use and sunscreen. Avoid aggressive squeezing.
warnings: Do not combine daily strong acids with retinoids.

ingredients.name: Salicylic Acid
ingredients.benefit: Commonly used to help the look of congested pores.
ingredients.caution: Can dry; follow with moisturizer.

whiteheads.name: Whiteheads
whiteheads.description: Closed clogged pores that look like small bumps.
whiteheads.usage_guidance: A BHA and, if tolerated later, a retinoid-style ingredient. Introduce one active at a time.
warnings: Adapalene can irritate; start 2–3 nights weekly and use moisturizer.
Avoid using adapalene with strong acids on the same night.

ingredients.name: Salicylic Acid
ingredients.benefit: May help the appearance of clogged-looking bumps.
ingredients.caution: Do not pair with retinoids on the same night when starting.

ingredients.name: Adapalene
ingredients.benefit: A retinoid-style ingredient commonly used for congestion; introduce slowly.
ingredients.usage: Night only, 2–3 times weekly at first, moisturizer after (sandwich method if sensitive).
ingredients.caution: Increases sun sensitivity. Not for use in pregnancy unless a clinician advises. Over-the-counter where available; this is not a prescription.

redness.name: Redness
redness.description: Skin that looks flushed, irritated, or easily reddened.
aliases: my skin is red and irritated
redness.usage_guidance: Simplify the routine: gentle cleanser, soothing serum, barrier moisturizer, mineral-leaning sunscreen if tolerated.
warnings: Skip fragrance, menthol, and strong acids until calm. Spreading redness with fever needs medical care.

ingredients.name: Centella Asiatica
ingredients.benefit: Commonly used to support a calmer-looking feel.
ingredients.usage: Morning and night in serum or cream.

ingredients.name: Azelaic Acid
ingredients.benefit: May help the appearance of redness for some people.
ingredients.caution: Can tingle; stop if burning persists.

ingredients.name: Panthenol
ingredients.benefit: Can support comfort and a less tight-feeling surface.

sensitive_skin.name: Sensitive Skin
sensitive_skin.description: Skin that stings, itches, or reacts easily to products.
sensitive_skin.usage_guidance: Fragrance-free basics. Patch test new products. Add only one new product per 1–2 weeks.
warnings: Avoid retinoids and strong acids until the barrier feels stable.

ingredients.name: Ceramides
ingredients.benefit: May help support a more comfortable barrier.

ingredients.name: Panthenol
ingredients.benefit: Commonly used to soothe a tight or reactive feel.

ingredients.name: Centella Asiatica
ingredients.benefit: Can support a calmer-looking appearance.
ingredients.usage: Leave-on products, twice daily if tolerated.

fine_lines.name: Fine Lines
fine_lines.description: Lines that look more visible with dryness or over time.
fine_lines.usage_guidance: Daily SPF, hydration, then a retinoid at night if tolerated. Do not combine with strong acids on the same night.
warnings: Retinol can irritate; start low and slow.
Retinoids are generally avoided in pregnancy unless a clinician advises.

ingredients.name: Retinol
ingredients.benefit: Commonly used to support the look of texture and fine lines over time.
ingredients.usage: Night only, 2–3 times weekly at first, moisturizer after. SPF the next day.
ingredients.caution: Do not use with AHA/BHA on the same night when starting. Avoid if pregnant unless advised by a clinician.

ingredients.name: Peptides
ingredients.benefit: May support a smoother-looking feel with low irritation for many people.

ingredients.name: Hyaluronic Acid
ingredients.benefit: Can plump the look of dryness-related lines by adding water.

rough_texture.name: Rough Texture
rough_texture.description: Skin that feels bumpy or uneven to the touch.
rough_texture.usage_guidance: Gentle chemical exfoliation 1–2 times weekly, not daily. Always moisturize and use SPF.
warnings: Do not use glycolic, lactic, and salicylic acids together on the same night. Do not pair with retinol at first.

ingredients.name: Lactic Acid
ingredients.benefit: A gentler AHA that may help the look of rough, dull-feeling skin.
ingredients.usage: Once weekly at night to start, 5–10% if tolerated.
ingredients.caution: Sun sensitivity; SPF next day. Not with retinoids same night.

ingredients.name: Glycolic Acid
ingredients.benefit: Commonly used for the appearance of uneven texture.
ingredients.usage: Once weekly at night if lactic acid is tolerated; do not stack with other acids.
ingredients.caution: More irritating than lactic acid. Skip if sensitive or barrier-compromised.

ingredients.name: Salicylic Acid
ingredients.benefit: Can support smoother-looking congested areas.
ingredients.usage: Alternate weeks or different nights from AHAs.
ingredients.caution: Do not combine with other strong exfoliants the same night.

enlarged_pores.name: Enlarged-Looking Pores
enlarged_pores.description: Pores that look more visible, often with oil or congestion.
enlarged_pores.usage_guidance: Oil-balancing and BHA ingredients are commonly used. Pores do not permanently 'close'.
warnings: Avoid harsh scrubs that can make pores look more pronounced.

ingredients.name: Niacinamide
ingredients.benefit: May help the appearance of pores over time.

ingredients.name: Salicylic Acid
ingredients.benefit: Commonly used to help keep pores looking clearer.
ingredients.caution: Can dry; buffer with moisturizer.

barrier_damage.name: Barrier Damage
barrier_damage.description: Skin that feels raw, tight, or stings after many products—often from over-exfoliation.
barrier_damage.usage_guidance: Pause actives. Use a bland cleanser, ceramide moisturizer, and sunscreen only until comfortable.
warnings: Pause retinol, vitamin C, and acids until stinging settles.

ingredients.name: Ceramides
ingredients.benefit: Can support barrier comfort.

ingredients.name: Panthenol
ingredients.benefit: May help a less tight, less stingy feel.

ingredients.name: Centella Asiatica
ingredients.benefit: Commonly used in soothing routines.

sun_damage.name: Sun Damage (appearance)
sun_damage.description: Uneven tone or texture that people often associate with sun exposure. Not a medical diagnosis.
sun_damage.usage_guidance: Daily broad-spectrum SPF is the priority. Antioxidants in the morning may support appearance.
warnings: This is not a diagnosis of photodamage or skin cancer. Changing moles need a clinician.

ingredients.name: Vitamin C
ingredients.benefit: Commonly used in the morning to support a brighter-looking tone alongside sunscreen.
ingredients.caution: Can sting.

ingredients.name: Niacinamide
ingredients.benefit: May help the look of uneven tone.

ingredients.name: Retinol
ingredients.benefit: Can support the look of texture at night if the barrier is healthy.
ingredients.caution: SPF next day. Avoid in pregnancy unless advised.

dark_circles.name: Dark Circles
dark_circles.description: Under-eye area that looks darker. Many causes exist (genetics, sleep, shadowing).
dark_circles.usage_guidance: Gentle hydration. Caffeine or peptides in eye products are optional. Do not use strong acids near the eyes.
warnings: Sudden dark circles with swelling or pain should be checked medically. Sleep and allergies also matter.

ingredients.name: Hyaluronic Acid
ingredients.benefit: May help the look of dryness that can make shadows more obvious.
ingredients.caution: Keep out of the eye.

ingredients.name: Peptides
ingredients.benefit: Sometimes used to support a smoother-looking under-eye area.

ingredients.name: Niacinamide
ingredients.benefit: Can support the look of tone for some people.
ingredients.caution: Stop if stinging.

under_eye_puffiness.name: Under-Eye Puffiness
under_eye_puffiness.description: Puffy-looking under-eyes. Often related to sleep, salt, or allergies—not a diagnosis.
under_eye_puffiness.usage_guidance: Cool compresses, sleep, and a gentle hydrating eye product. Caffeine serums are optional.
warnings: Sudden swelling with pain, vision change, or fever needs urgent care.

ingredients.name: Caffeine (topical)
ingredients.benefit: Sometimes used to support a less puffy-looking appearance temporarily.
ingredients.caution: Keep out of the eye.

ingredients.name: Peptides
ingredients.benefit: May support a smoother-looking eye area.

ingredients.name: Hyaluronic Acid
ingredients.benefit: Can help if puffiness is accompanied by dryness.
ingredients.caution: Too much product can pill.

acne_scars.name: Acne Scars (appearance)
acne_scars.description: Textured or marked-looking areas after breakouts. True scarring should be assessed by a dermatologist.
acne_scars.usage_guidance: Home care may support the look of marks and texture. Indented scars often need in-clinic options.
warnings: Do not promise scar removal. See a dermatologist for pitted or widespread scarring.

ingredients.name: Niacinamide
ingredients.benefit: May help the look of leftover marks.

ingredients.name: Azelaic Acid
ingredients.benefit: Can support the appearance of discoloration after breakouts.
ingredients.caution: May tingle.

ingredients.name: Retinol
ingredients.benefit: Sometimes used to support the look of texture over time.
ingredients.usage: Night, slowly, with SPF by day.
ingredients.caution: Irritating; not with acids same night at first.
